title: The cruiser that rolled over

facts.text: By late 1942 Naples had become the Regia Marina's most important base. Taranto was now too exposed, and the fleet's big ships had moved to the bay below Vesuvius.

One of them was the light cruiser Muzio Attendolo. On 13 August 1942, during the battle for the Pedestal convoy to Malta, the British submarine Unbroken had torpedoed her and blown off her bow. She limped to Messina and then Naples for repair.

On 4 December 1942, U.S. B-24 Liberators of the Ninth Air Force's 98th and 376th Bombardment Groups, flying from Egypt, attacked the harbor. It was the first USAAF raid on Italy. The official chronology counts 20 bombers; other accounts say 24.
The bombers came over at about 20,000 feet. Anti aircraft guns opened fire at 4.40 p.m., and the raid lasted about an hour.
One or two bombs struck Muzio Attendolo amidships. Power failed, water poured in below the waterline and fires raged aft. Of the three cruisers hit, she was the worst damaged.
The cruisers Raimondo Montecuccoli and Eugenio di Savoia were also hit. Montecuccoli took a bomb by her funnel. On the battleship Littorio, one sailor was killed.
Her crew fought the flooding into the night. At 9.17 p.m. a false air raid alarm sent the damage control parties to shelter, and they did not get back for more than an hour.
At about 10.19 p.m. Muzio Attendolo rolled over almost completely and settled on the bottom at her moorings.
The Italian navy's veterans' association puts the dead aboard her at 188. Other accounts give 188 as the minimum for all three cruisers together; the full toll is not known.

Bombs also fell on the city, hitting houses, churches, hospitals and offices, among them the main post office and the area around Porta Nolana. Estimates of the civilian dead range from about 150 to about 900.
It was only the beginning. Naples would be bombed again and again until the Allies took it in October 1943, and between 20,000 and 25,000 of its people died in the air raids of the war.

declassified.fact: Italy judged Muzio Attendolo repairable in 10 to 12 months, but salvage never began before the armistice, and the Allies used her overturned hull as a dock. After the war the navy thought of rebuilding her as an anti aircraft cruiser, then raised her and scrapped her.
